question.leadin: This ruler founded the Achaemenid [ah-KEE-men-id] Empire, which successfully grew by supporting local rulers as satraps and respecting local customs.
question.text: Name this "Great" Persian ruler of the sixth century BCE who ended the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: This victor of the Battle of Thymbra passed the Edict of Restoration, which granted the Jews religious tolerance, ending the Babylonian Captivity.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the role of the pythia in Ancient Greece.
swap.text: The second Persian invasion of Greece was led by this monarch, the son of Darius I. While victorious at Thermopylae, his armies were defeated at Platea after they burned Athens.
swap.clue: This man ordered the building of the Gate of All Nations, enhancing his father's building projects at Persepolis.

question.leadin: Though Susa was the official capital of this empire, Persepolis was the ceremonial capital.
question.text: Name this empire founded by Cyrus the Great in modern-day Iran. Kings named Darius and Xerxes led this empire.
question.clue: Another ruler of this empire used camels to win the Battle of Thymbra against Croesus of Lydia, and overthrew the earlier Median Empire.

swap.leadin: This man born as Codomannus took the throne following the scheming of the Vizier Bagoas.
swap.text: Name this final ruler of the Persian Achaemenid Empire who lost the battles of Issus and Gaugamela.
swap.clue: This monarch was served by Memnon of Rhodes, and this man's Cardaces were completely destroyed at a engagement in which his wife Stateria I was captured, that was the Battle of Issus.

question.text: This Persian dynasty that succeeded the Parthians successfully besieged Constantinople in 626 CᐧE. Its first leader was Ardashir I.
question.clue: Its last great ruler was deposed by Bahram, but with the help of Emperor Maurice regained the throne.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about conflicts within the Byzantine Empire.
swap.text: The Byzantine Empire nearly ended during an early 7th century war with this empire, at the time led by Khosrow II. This empire was based in the same region as the earlier Achaemenid Empire.
swap.answerHtml: Sasanian Empire [or Neo-Persian Empire or Empire of the Iranians; accept “Sassanid” in place of Sasanian]
swap.clue: The main feature remaining from this empire's capital is the Taq Kasra brickwork vault.

question.text: This Elamite city served as the capital of Cyrus the Great before Xerxes' father Darius I built a new one at Persepolis.
question.clue: A polity that called itself Haltamti transferred its capital from Anshan to this city, and this "great holy city" suffered a brutal sack by Ashurbanipal.

swap.leadin: The Achaeminid or Persian Empire was established by Cyrus the Great in the sixth century BCE after he overthrew the Median Empire.
swap.text: Darius the Great created 20 provinces in the Persian Empire. Each province had one of these people that were appointed by Darius himself.
swap.clue: 26 positions with this title were established around 580 BCE, a number that later increased to 36 according to the Behistun Inscription.

question.text: The Ten Thousand were originally hired to fight for Cyrus the Younger against his brother Artaxerxes II. Cyrus the Younger died in this battle when his forces were betrayed by Tissaphernes.
question.clue: Clearchus took command of one side's army after this battle, but was himself later murdered at a banquet given by Tissaphernes.

swap.leadin: The Hall of Hundred Columns in this city has the same dimensions as Athens's Odeon.
swap.text: Identify this ceremonial capital in the Zagros Mountains, home to the Apadana Palace built by Darius I.
swap.clue: In this home of a hundred-columned throne room, the Gate of All Nations led to the apadana palace.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the generals who carved up Alexander the Great's empire after his death, the Diadochi.
question.text: This man managed to grab the lion's share of the empire, taking Mesopotamia, Persia, and Bactria. He later fought an unsuccessful war with Chandragupta Maurya.
question.clue: This ruler, one of Alexander the Great's successors, who established a namesake Hellenistic kingdom in western Asia and was succeeded by his son Antiochus I.

swap.leadin: A ruler with this name had the Lakhmid king Al Nu'man III executed.
swap.text: Give this name of a Sassanid shahanshah who then annexed the Lakhmid kingdom. An earlier shahanshah of this name went to war with Justinian after his allies raided the Lakhmids, who were then Sassanid vassals.
swap.answerHtml: Khosrau [accept Khosrau I, Khosrau II, Khosrau Anushirawan, Khosrau the Just, or Chosroes]
swap.clue: The second Sassanid ruler with this name held a truce with the Byzantine Empire because of his friendship with the Emperor Maurice, which lasted until Maurice was killed. The first began an "Eternal Peace" because of a bribe from Justinian, which lasted until that ruler got bored.

question.leadin: This city may have been the largest in the world for a period before it was eclipsed by the growth of nearby Baghdad.
question.text: Name this ancient city on the bank of the Tigris. This major commercial center was the capital of both the Parthian and Sassanian empires.
question.clue: This city was known by Arabs as "al- Mada'in" or "the cities" due to its many suburbs, one of which was sarcastically dubbed "better than Antioch," while another was home to the patriarch of the Nestorian church.

swap.text: A branch of the Royal Road also serviced this Achaemenid summer capital whose royal treasury was looted by Alexander. According to Herodotus, Deioces ("day-OH-seas") legendarily built seven multicolored walls around this first capital of the Median Empire.
swap.answerHtml: Ecbatana [or Ecbatan or Hagmatāna or Ahmadān or Agamtanu or Agmadana; accept Hamedan, Iran]
swap.clue: After his son Philotas was caught conspiring against Alexander the Great, the Macedonian general Parmenion was killed in this city.

question.text: Septimus Severus defeated the fifth Parthian emperor with this name. The sixth emperor of this name would be defeated by the Sassanids in the early third century CE.
question.clue: A man of this name fought a war against Izates and perhaps codified the Avesta as part of an Iranian Revival. The sixth and last Parthian king of this name faced trouble from the Sassanid Adrashir I.

swap.text: Along with Hecatompylos, Susa and Ctesiphon, Ecbatana was a summer capital used by the Arsacid rulers of this Empire.
swap.clue: This Persian dynasty supplanted by the Sassanids, whose General Surena served Marcus Crassus a molten gold cocktail after using his vast army of horse archers to win the Battle of Carrhae.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a kingdom in Asia FTPE.
question.text: The son of Cyaxares and grandfather of Cyrus the Great, he ruled as the last king of the Medes until Cyrus overthrew him.
question.clue: Cyrus began his conquest by overthrowing this Median king, the son of Cyaxares, and, according to Herodotus, Cyrus' grandfather.

swap.leadin: This man made an alliance with Nabopolassar, which resulted in the destruction of Nineveh and the Neo-Assyrian Empire.
swap.text: Name this third and greatest king of the Medes, according to Herodotus. At the very end of his long reign, he fought the Battle of Halys River against Lydia, which infamously ended with an eclipse. After that, he was succeeded by the final Median king, Astyages.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the last Himyarite king, Abraha's son Ma'd-Karib.
question.text: Ma'd Karib was assisted by this Sassanid shahanshah during a later Axumite invasion of Himyar, which saw this monarch's general Vahrez win the Battle of Hadhramaut. Earlier, he concluded the Eternal Peace with Justinian the Great.
question.clue: This Sasanian emperor who succeeded Kavad I. Most historians believe that Yemen came under Sassanid rule during his reign.

swap.text: Valerian lost at Edessa to the first Sassanid ruler of this name, the son of founder Ardeshir I, who prompted Gordian's murder by Philip the Arab after winning the Battle of Misiche but saw his harem raided by Balista. The second ruler of this name fought Pap and Arshak II of Armenia and killed Julian the Apostate outside Ctesiphon.
swap.clue: A king with this name built a namesake city on the road between Estakhr and Ctesiphon.
